work.title: Twelfth Night; or, What You Will
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Enter Viola and Clown with a tabor.

lines.text: Save thee, friend, and thy music. Dost thou live by thy tabor?
lines.plainText: Save thee friend and thy music Dost thou live by thy tabor

lines.text: No, sir, I live by the church.
lines.plainText: No sir I live by the church

lines.text: Art thou a churchman?
lines.plainText: Art thou a churchman

lines.text: No such matter, sir. I do live by the church, for I do live at my house, and my house doth stand by the church.
lines.plainText: No such matter sir I do live by the church for I do live at my house and my house doth stand by the church

lines.text: So thou mayst say the king lies by a beggar, if a beggar dwell near him; or the church stands by thy tabor, if thy tabor stand by the church.
lines.plainText: So thou mayst say the king lies by a beggar if a beggar dwell near him or the church stands by thy tabor if thy tabor stand by the church

lines.text: You have said, sir. To see this age! A sentence is but a chev'ril glove to a good wit. How quickly the wrong side may be turned outward!
lines.plainText: You have said sir To see this age A sentence is but a chev'ril glove to a good wit How quickly the wrong side may be turned outward

lines.text: Nay, that's certain; they that dally nicely with words may quickly make them wanton.
lines.plainText: Nay that's certain they that dally nicely with words may quickly make them wanton

lines.text: I would, therefore, my sister had had no name, sir.
lines.plainText: I would therefore my sister had had no name sir

lines.text: Why, man?
lines.plainText: Why man

lines.text: Why, sir, her name's a word; and to dally with that word might make my sister wanton. But indeed, words are very rascals, since bonds disgraced them.
lines.plainText: Why sir her name's a word and to dally with that word might make my sister wanton But indeed words are very rascals since bonds disgraced them

lines.text: Thy reason, man?
lines.plainText: Thy reason man

lines.text: Troth, sir, I can yield you none without words, and words are grown so false, I am loath to prove reason with them.
lines.plainText: Troth sir I can yield you none without words and words are grown so false I am loath to prove reason with them

lines.text: I warrant thou art a merry fellow, and car'st for nothing.
lines.plainText: I warrant thou art a merry fellow and car'st for nothing

lines.text: Not so, sir, I do care for something. But in my conscience, sir, I do not care for you. If that be to care for nothing, sir, I would it would make you invisible.
lines.plainText: Not so sir I do care for something But in my conscience sir I do not care for you If that be to care for nothing sir I would it would make you invisible

lines.text: Art not thou the Lady Olivia's fool?
lines.plainText: Art not thou the Lady Olivia's fool

lines.text: No, indeed, sir; the Lady Olivia has no folly. She will keep no fool, sir, till she be married, and fools are as like husbands as pilchards are to herrings, the husband's the bigger. I am indeed not her fool, but her corrupter of words.
lines.plainText: No indeed sir the Lady Olivia has no folly She will keep no fool sir till she be married and fools are as like husbands as pilchards are to herrings the husband's the bigger I am indeed not her fool but her corrupter of words

lines.text: I saw thee late at the Count Orsino's.
lines.plainText: I saw thee late at the Count Orsino's

lines.text: Foolery, sir, does walk about the orb like the sun; it shines everywhere. I would be sorry, sir, but the fool should be as oft with your master as with my mistress. I think I saw your wisdom there.
lines.plainText: Foolery sir does walk about the orb like the sun it shines everywhere I would be sorry sir but the fool should be as oft with your master as with my mistress I think I saw your wisdom there

lines.text: Nay, and thou pass upon me, I'll no more with thee. Hold, there's expenses for thee.
lines.plainText: Nay and thou pass upon me I'll no more with thee Hold there's expenses for thee

lines.text: Now Jove, in his next commodity of hair, send thee a beard!
lines.plainText: Now Jove in his next commodity of hair send thee a beard

lines.text: By my troth, I'll tell thee, I am almost sick for one, though I would not have it grow on my chin. Is thy lady within?
lines.plainText: By my troth I'll tell thee I am almost sick for one though I would not have it grow on my chin Is thy lady within

lines.text: Would not a pair of these have bred, sir?
lines.plainText: Would not a pair of these have bred sir

lines.text: Yes, being kept together, and put to use.
lines.plainText: Yes being kept together and put to use

lines.text: I would play Lord Pandarus of Phrygia, sir, to bring a Cressida to this Troilus.
lines.plainText: I would play Lord Pandarus of Phrygia sir to bring a Cressida to this Troilus

lines.text: I understand you, sir; 'tis well begged.
lines.plainText: I understand you sir 'tis well begged

lines.text: The matter, I hope, is not great, sir, begging but a beggar: Cressida was a beggar. My lady is within, sir. I will conster to them whence you come; who you are and what you would are out of my welkin. I might say "element", but the word is overworn.
lines.plainText: The matter I hope is not great sir begging but a beggar Cressida was a beggar My lady is within sir I will conster to them whence you come who you are and what you would are out of my welkin I might say element but the word is overworn

lines.text: This fellow is wise enough to play the fool,
lines.plainText: This fellow is wise enough to play the fool

lines.text: And to do that well, craves a kind of wit:
lines.plainText: And to do that well craves a kind of wit

lines.text: He must observe their mood on whom he jests,
lines.plainText: He must observe their mood on whom he jests

lines.text: The quality of persons, and the time,
lines.plainText: The quality of persons and the time

lines.text: And like the haggard, check at every feather
lines.plainText: And like the haggard check at every feather

lines.text: That comes before his eye. This is a practice
lines.plainText: That comes before his eye This is a practice

lines.text: As full of labour as a wise man's art:
lines.plainText: As full of labour as a wise man's art

lines.text: For folly, that he wisely shows, is fit;
lines.plainText: For folly that he wisely shows is fit

lines.text: But wise men, folly-fall'n, quite taint their wit.
lines.plainText: But wise men follyfall'n quite taint their wit

content.text: Enter Sir Toby and Sir Andrew.

lines.text: Save you, gentleman.
lines.plainText: Save you gentleman

lines.text: And you, sir.
lines.plainText: And you sir

lines.text: Dieu vous garde, monsieur.
lines.plainText: Dieu vous garde monsieur

lines.text: Et vous aussi; votre serviteur.
lines.plainText: Et vous aussi votre serviteur

lines.text: I hope, sir, you are, and I am yours.
lines.plainText: I hope sir you are and I am yours

lines.text: Will you encounter the house? My niece is desirous you should enter, if your trade be to her.
lines.plainText: Will you encounter the house My niece is desirous you should enter if your trade be to her

lines.text: I am bound to your niece, sir, I mean, she is the list of my voyage.
lines.plainText: I am bound to your niece sir I mean she is the list of my voyage

lines.text: Taste your legs, sir, put them to motion.
lines.plainText: Taste your legs sir put them to motion

lines.text: My legs do better understand me, sir, than I understand what you mean by bidding me taste my legs.
lines.plainText: My legs do better understand me sir than I understand what you mean by bidding me taste my legs

lines.text: I mean, to go, sir, to enter.
lines.plainText: I mean to go sir to enter

lines.text: I will answer you with gait and entrance: but we are prevented.
lines.plainText: I will answer you with gait and entrance but we are prevented

lines.text: That youth's a rare courtier. 'Rain odours,' well.
lines.plainText: That youth's a rare courtier 'Rain odours' well

lines.text: My matter hath no voice, lady, but to your own most pregnant and vouchsafed ear.
lines.plainText: My matter hath no voice lady but to your own most pregnant and vouchsafed ear

lines.text: 'Odours,' 'pregnant,' and 'vouchsafed.'—I'll get 'em all three ready.
lines.plainText: 'Odours' 'pregnant' and 'vouchsafed'I'll get 'em all three ready

lines.text: Let the garden door be shut, and leave me to my hearing.
lines.plainText: Let the garden door be shut and leave me to my hearing

content.text: [Exeunt Sir Toby, Sir Andrew and Maria.]

lines.text: My duty, madam, and most humble service.
lines.plainText: My duty madam and most humble service

lines.text: What is your name?
lines.plainText: What is your name

lines.text: Cesario is your servant's name, fair princess.
lines.plainText: Cesario is your servant's name fair princess

lines.text: My servant, sir! 'Twas never merry world,
lines.plainText: My servant sir 'Twas never merry world

lines.text: Since lowly feigning was call'd compliment:
lines.plainText: Since lowly feigning was call'd compliment

lines.text: Y'are servant to the Count Orsino, youth.
lines.plainText: Y'are servant to the Count Orsino youth

lines.text: And he is yours, and his must needs be yours.
lines.plainText: And he is yours and his must needs be yours

lines.text: Your servant's servant is your servant, madam.
lines.plainText: Your servant's servant is your servant madam

lines.text: For him, I think not on him: for his thoughts,
lines.plainText: For him I think not on him for his thoughts

lines.text: Would they were blanks rather than fill'd with me!
lines.plainText: Would they were blanks rather than fill'd with me

lines.text: Madam, I come to whet your gentle thoughts
lines.plainText: Madam I come to whet your gentle thoughts

lines.text: On his behalf.
lines.plainText: On his behalf

lines.text: O, by your leave, I pray you.
lines.plainText: O by your leave I pray you

lines.text: I bade you never speak again of him.
lines.plainText: I bade you never speak again of him

lines.text: But would you undertake another suit,
lines.plainText: But would you undertake another suit

lines.text: I had rather hear you to solicit that
lines.plainText: I had rather hear you to solicit that

lines.text: Than music from the spheres.
lines.plainText: Than music from the spheres

lines.text: Dear lady—
lines.plainText: Dear lady

lines.text: Give me leave, beseech you. I did send,
lines.plainText: Give me leave beseech you I did send

lines.text: After the last enchantment you did here,
lines.plainText: After the last enchantment you did here

lines.text: A ring in chase of you. So did I abuse
lines.plainText: A ring in chase of you So did I abuse

lines.text: Myself, my servant, and, I fear me, you.
lines.plainText: Myself my servant and I fear me you

lines.text: Under your hard construction must I sit;
lines.plainText: Under your hard construction must I sit

lines.text: To force that on you in a shameful cunning,
lines.plainText: To force that on you in a shameful cunning

lines.text: Which you knew none of yours. What might you think?
lines.plainText: Which you knew none of yours What might you think

lines.text: Have you not set mine honour at the stake,
lines.plainText: Have you not set mine honour at the stake

lines.text: And baited it with all th' unmuzzled thoughts
lines.plainText: And baited it with all th' unmuzzled thoughts

lines.text: That tyrannous heart can think? To one of your receiving
lines.plainText: That tyrannous heart can think To one of your receiving

lines.text: Enough is shown. A cypress, not a bosom,
lines.plainText: Enough is shown A cypress not a bosom

lines.text: Hides my heart: so let me hear you speak.
lines.plainText: Hides my heart so let me hear you speak

lines.text: I pity you.
lines.plainText: I pity you

lines.text: That's a degree to love.
lines.plainText: That's a degree to love

lines.text: No, not a grize; for 'tis a vulgar proof
lines.plainText: No not a grize for 'tis a vulgar proof

lines.text: That very oft we pity enemies.
lines.plainText: That very oft we pity enemies

lines.text: Why then methinks 'tis time to smile again.
lines.plainText: Why then methinks 'tis time to smile again

lines.text: O world, how apt the poor are to be proud!
lines.plainText: O world how apt the poor are to be proud

lines.text: If one should be a prey, how much the better
lines.plainText: If one should be a prey how much the better

lines.text: To fall before the lion than the wolf! [Clock strikes.]
lines.plainText: To fall before the lion than the wolf Clock strikes

lines.text: The clock upbraids me with the waste of time.
lines.plainText: The clock upbraids me with the waste of time

lines.text: Be not afraid, good youth, I will not have you.
lines.plainText: Be not afraid good youth I will not have you

lines.text: And yet, when wit and youth is come to harvest,
lines.plainText: And yet when wit and youth is come to harvest

lines.text: Your wife is like to reap a proper man.
lines.plainText: Your wife is like to reap a proper man

lines.text: There lies your way, due west.
lines.plainText: There lies your way due west

lines.text: Then westward ho!
lines.plainText: Then westward ho

lines.text: Grace and good disposition attend your ladyship!
lines.plainText: Grace and good disposition attend your ladyship

lines.text: You'll nothing, madam, to my lord by me?
lines.plainText: You'll nothing madam to my lord by me

lines.text: Stay:
lines.plainText: Stay

lines.text: I prithee tell me what thou think'st of me.
lines.plainText: I prithee tell me what thou think'st of me

lines.text: That you do think you are not what you are.
lines.plainText: That you do think you are not what you are

lines.text: If I think so, I think the same of you.
lines.plainText: If I think so I think the same of you

lines.text: Then think you right; I am not what I am.
lines.plainText: Then think you right I am not what I am

lines.text: I would you were as I would have you be.
lines.plainText: I would you were as I would have you be

lines.text: Would it be better, madam, than I am?
lines.plainText: Would it be better madam than I am

lines.text: I wish it might, for now I am your fool.
lines.plainText: I wish it might for now I am your fool

lines.text: O what a deal of scorn looks beautiful
lines.plainText: O what a deal of scorn looks beautiful

lines.text: In the contempt and anger of his lip!
lines.plainText: In the contempt and anger of his lip

lines.text: A murd'rous guilt shows not itself more soon
lines.plainText: A murd'rous guilt shows not itself more soon

lines.text: Than love that would seem hid. Love's night is noon.
lines.plainText: Than love that would seem hid Love's night is noon

lines.text: Cesario, by the roses of the spring,
lines.plainText: Cesario by the roses of the spring

lines.text: By maidhood, honour, truth, and everything,
lines.plainText: By maidhood honour truth and everything

lines.text: I love thee so, that maugre all thy pride,
lines.plainText: I love thee so that maugre all thy pride

lines.text: Nor wit nor reason can my passion hide.
lines.plainText: Nor wit nor reason can my passion hide

lines.text: Do not extort thy reasons from this clause,
lines.plainText: Do not extort thy reasons from this clause

lines.text: For that I woo, thou therefore hast no cause;
lines.plainText: For that I woo thou therefore hast no cause

lines.text: But rather reason thus with reason fetter:
lines.plainText: But rather reason thus with reason fetter

lines.text: Love sought is good, but given unsought is better.
lines.plainText: Love sought is good but given unsought is better

lines.text: By innocence I swear, and by my youth,
lines.plainText: By innocence I swear and by my youth

lines.text: I have one heart, one bosom, and one truth,
lines.plainText: I have one heart one bosom and one truth

lines.text: And that no woman has; nor never none
lines.plainText: And that no woman has nor never none

lines.text: Shall mistress be of it, save I alone.
lines.plainText: Shall mistress be of it save I alone

lines.plainText: And so adieu good madam never more

lines.text: Will I my master's tears to you deplore.
lines.plainText: Will I my master's tears to you deplore
